epigraph: The root holds the line against the dark fire.
vignette: The palace-tree stands at the center of the Verdant claim. Its bark is polished glass. Its leaves are solid gold. It does not sway. It does not breathe. It simply is. The Umbral armies press against its base. They bring obsidian blades and hungry embers. They strike the trunk. The impact makes no sound. The ground shudders. A crack appears in the glass bark. For a moment, the gold leaves dim. The Verdant faith wavers. The soldiers hesitate. Their conviction falters. The crack seals. The leaves shine brighter. The Umbral ground turns to ash. The ash blows away. The tree remains. It is the anchor. If you unwrite this tree, the Verdant truth vanishes from Limen. The forests wither. The glass shatters. The permanence ends. The threshold falls to appetite. The tree is the seed. It holds the line. It writes the world true. You cannot move it. You can only try to erase it. The ground believes in the tree. The tree believes in the ground. This is the war. This is the peace.
codex_note: Scholars note that the palace-tree does not grow but persists, serving as the singular ontological anchor for all Verdant reality in the threshold.
